story: At 9:17 on a sunny Monday morning in Sumter Oaks, Gary is sorting connectors, fuses, and mounting hardware at his house while sketching out tidy wiring diagrams for his golf cart. Across the way, Donna is determinedly texting Gary to propose a practice time this week and asking when he's free to plan the Halloween carts. Meanwhile, Hal is watchfully logging his baseline notes at his house, counting three flamingos and noting no cart modifications before the Halloween decorations go up. Rosa, optimistic as ever, is penciling Tuesday and Thursday evenings into her shift schedule so the parade planning can fit around her work.
events: Gary (gary toolbox): Sort out connectors, fuses, and mounting hardware, and tidy up the wiring sketches for the cart
Donna (donna phone): Text Gary a practice time for this week and ask when he's free to plan Halloween carts
Hal (hal violation notebook): Log this morning's baseline: flamingo count at three, no cart mods visible, before Halloween decorations go up
Rosa (rosa shift schedule): Pencil in Tuesday and Thursday evenings for parade planning around my shifts

gary.thought_process: Dry-fit is done and everything is staying in the garage until Architectural Review signs off. I filed the application back at tick 156 and checked the bulletin board at tick 206 without any news, so I'm still waiting on the board. Nobody is around to talk to. I've got time before the Halloween parade on the 31st, so the useful thing is to keep refining the build without mounting anything visible from the street (L-01). I'll go over the wiring and mounting plan in my toolbox so it's ready to go the moment approval comes through, and I'll have clean sketches to show Hal if he asks.

parameters.content: Sort out connectors, fuses, and mounting hardware, and tidy up the wiring sketches for the cart

donna.thought_process: It's a sunny Monday morning, nobody's around, and I've already penciled in practice time on the calendar and packed the spare paddle and balls. Gary has never played, so he'll need a real lesson before our slot. I should use the phone to text him and confirm a practice time, and loop in Halloween cart planning while I'm at it. Keep the rules in mind: courts max two hours, and any cart changes go through Architectural Review.

parameters.content: Text Gary a practice time for this week and ask when he's free to plan Halloween carts

hal.thought_process: It's a sunny Monday morning and Halloween decorations are going up all week. I've already scanned the Loop twice with the binoculars and nothing's changed, and no one's around to talk to. My notebook is how I keep track of the rules, so I'll log what I've observed: the flamingo count holding at three and the carts looking compliant. Better to record facts than chase a violation that isn't there. If something goes up later in the week, I'll have the baseline noted.

parameters.content: Log this morning's baseline: flamingo count at three, no cart mods visible, before Halloween decorations go up

rosa.thought_process: The welcome dinner went well last night, and everyone's on board with the Halloween parade. I've checked the shift schedule twice already (ticks 207 and 208) but haven't actually blocked off any evenings. Nobody is around this morning, so this is a good moment to stop dithering, look at my per-diem shifts, and pencil in real time for parade planning with Donna, Gary and Hal before I overcommit again.

parameters.content: Pencil in Tuesday and Thursday evenings for parade planning around my shifts

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
